title: Philip S. Boonstra, PhD
text:
I’m an Associate Professor in the Department of Biostatistics at the University of Michigan. I’ve been a faculty member here since 2013. I have my MS and PhD in Biostatistics, also from UM. I previously studied Mathematics and Political Science at Calvin College (now University) in Grand Rapids, MI.
Some of my current research interests are in methods for combining or integrating statistical models, penalized likelihood, and applications in the areas of cancer clinical trials and Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO).
I also love teaching and working with students. You can see courses that I’ve taught on my teaching page. If you’re a prospective student, I’d be delighted to speak with you, but please know that I cannot admit students directly. You need to apply through our department’s admission process.
If you’re new to biostatistics or public health and want to learn more, go check out my three-course specialization with colleague Bhramar Mukherjee on Coursera: Data Science for Health Research
You can contact me at

philb@umich.example.edu

title: Teaching
text:
Biostatistics 699 is my department’s project-based capstone for MS students. I’ve co-taught this course with various colleagues every winter since 2019.



I recently developed and taught Public Health 345: Public Health Data Visualization for undergraduate students interested in public health. You can find my course slides here

title: Teaching
text:
Past classes

Biostatistics 619
Biostatistics 619 is a course on the design and analysis of clinical trials. I taught this for four years, most recently in winter 2018, when I expanded the course from two to three credits.


Biostatistics 591
I developed Biostatistics 591 as an introduction to the R statistical environment for students enrolled in the fully online MS in Population Health Sciences degree program at UM SPH. That program is now closed, so I no longer teach this course; however, if you’re interested in learning more about R please see my MOOC hosted on Coursera: Data Science for Health Research
